claim: Somatostatin is a peptide hormone that regulates endocrine systems by binding to G-protein-coupled somatostatin receptors.
source: Somatostatin is a peptide hormone that regulates endocrine systems by binding to G-protein-coupled somatostatin receptors.
evidence: This is a general statement about somatostatin function that is established in the scientific literature.

claim: SSTR2 is a human somatostatin receptor and is highly implicated in hormone disorders, cancers, and neurological diseases.
source: Somatostatin receptor 2 (SSTR2) is a human somatostatin receptor and is highly implicated in hormone disorders, cancers, and neurological diseases.
evidence: This statement is supported by established knowledge about SSTR2's role in disease.

claim: The authors determined a high-resolution cryo-EM structure of full-length human SSTR2 bound to SST-14 in complex with inhibitory G proteins.
source: Here, we report the high-resolution cryo-EM structure of full-length human SSTR2 bound to the agonist somatostatin (SST-14) in complex with inhibitory G (Gi) proteins.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental determination of this structure with detailed methods and results.

claim: Seven transmembrane helices of SSTR2 form a deep pocket for ligand binding.
source: Our structural and mutagenesis analyses show that seven transmembrane helices form a deep pocket for ligand binding and that SSTR2 recognizes the highly conserved Trp-Lys motif of SST-14 at the bottom of the pocket.
evidence: This is supported by the cryo-EM structure and mutagenesis experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: SSTR2 recognizes the highly conserved Trp-Lys motif of SST-14 at the bottom of the binding pocket.
source: Our structural and mutagenesis analyses show that seven transmembrane helices form a deep pocket for ligand binding and that SSTR2 recognizes the highly conserved Trp-Lys motif of SST-14 at the bottom of the pocket.
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis and mutagenesis data presented in the manuscript.

claim: SST was initially identified as an inhibitory hormone produced in hypothalamic neurons.
source: SST was initially identified as an inhibitory hormone produced in hypothalamic neurons, but it is also released in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract.
evidence: This is a historical fact about the discovery of somatostatin.

claim: SST is also released in the gastrointestinal tract.
source: SST was initially identified as an inhibitory hormone produced in hypothalamic neurons, but it is also released in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract.
evidence: This is established knowledge about somatostatin distribution.

claim: SST binds to G-protein-coupled somatostatin receptors, inhibiting adenylyl cyclase via inhibitory G-proteins.
source: SST binds to G-protein-coupled somatostatin receptors (SSTRs), inhibiting adenylyl cyclase via inhibitory G-proteins (Patel et al., 1994; Patel et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: SSTRs are class A G-protein-coupled receptors.
source: SSTRs are class A G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), and there are five isoforms (SSTR1–SSTR5) (Leu and Nandi, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: There are five SSTR isoforms (SSTR1–SSTR5).
source: SSTRs are class A G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), and there are five isoforms (SSTR1–SSTR5) (Leu and Nandi, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Each SSTR isoform is expressed in different tissues and organs and has a distinct function.
source: Each SSTR isoform is expressed in different tissues and organs and has a distinct function (Bartha and Győrffy, 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: SST inhibits the secretion of growth hormone from the pituitary gland.
source: SST inhibits the secretion of growth hormone from the pituitary gland, and SST secreted in the GI tract inhibits the secretion of GI hormones.
evidence: This is established knowledge about somatostatin function.

claim: SST secreted in the GI tract inhibits the secretion of GI hormones.
source: SST inhibits the secretion of growth hormone from the pituitary gland, and SST secreted in the GI tract inhibits the secretion of GI hormones.
evidence: This is established knowledge about somatostatin function.

claim: SST in the brain has been shown to modulate cortical circuits.
source: Furthermore, SST in the brain has been shown to modulate cortical circuits (Song et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The SST-SSTR axis is highly implicated in several human diseases, including acromegaly, cancers, and neurological disorders.
source: Therefore, the SST-SSTR axis is highly implicated in several human diseases, including acromegaly, cancers, and neurological disorders (Song et al., 2020; Song et al., 2021; Lamberts et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Several SST analogs, such as octreotide, lanreotide, and pasireotide, targeting SSTRs have been developed and are already in clinical use.
source: Several SST analogs, such as octreotide, lanreotide, and pasireotide, targeting SSTRs have been developed, and they are already in clinical use (Lamberts et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Acromegaly is caused by excessive production of growth hormone in the pituitary gland.
source: For example, acromegaly is caused by excessive production of growth hormone in the pituitary gland, and SST analogs such as octretotide and lanreotide are clinically used for treating acromegaly by exploiting the inhibitory role of SST via SSTR.
evidence: This is established medical knowledge.

claim: SST analogs such as octreotide and lanreotide are clinically used for treating acromegaly.
source: For example, acromegaly is caused by excessive production of growth hormone in the pituitary gland, and SST analogs such as octretotide and lanreotide are clinically used for treating acromegaly by exploiting the inhibitory role of SST via SSTR.
evidence: This is established medical knowledge.

claim: Currently used SST and its analogs have obscure binding specificity among SSTR isoforms.
source: However, the currently used SST and its analogs have obscure binding specificity among SSTR isoforms, making it difficult to develop means to modulate each isoform specifically while minimizing off-target effects.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of SST analog specificity.

claim: SSTR2 is mainly expressed in brain and endocrine tissues.
source: SSTR2 is mainly expressed in brain and endocrine tissues and is implicated in neuroendocrine tumors and Alzheimer's disease (Song et al., 2021; Uhlén et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: SSTR2 is implicated in neuroendocrine tumors and Alzheimer's disease.
source: SSTR2 is mainly expressed in brain and endocrine tissues and is implicated in neuroendocrine tumors and Alzheimer's disease (Song et al., 2021; Uhlén et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The overall resolution of the whole SSTR2-Gαi1/Gβ1γ2-scFv16 complex was estimated as 3.72 Å at 0.143 criteria of the gold standard FSC.
source: The overall resolution of the whole SSTR2-Gαi1/Gβ1γ2-scFv16 complex was estimated as 3.72 Å at 0.143 criteria of the gold standard FSC, and the resolutions of Body 1 and Body 2 were estimated as 3.65 and 3.22 Å, respectively.
evidence: This is a direct measurement from the cryo-EM data processing.

claim: The resolutions of Body 1 and Body 2 were estimated as 3.65 and 3.22 Å, respectively.
source: The overall resolution of the whole SSTR2-Gαi1/Gβ1γ2-scFv16 complex was estimated as 3.72 Å at 0.143 criteria of the gold standard FSC, and the resolutions of Body 1 and Body 2 were estimated as 3.65 and 3.22 Å, respectively.
evidence: This is a direct measurement from the cryo-EM data processing.

claim: The C-terminal helix of Gαi1 is inserted inside of the seven transmembrane helices forming hydrophobic interactions with TM 5–7 helices.
source: In the structure, the C-terminal helix of Gαi1 is inserted inside of the seven transmembrane (TM) helices forming hydrophobic interactions with TM 5–7 helices (Figure 1B), and scFv16 interacts with the N-terminal helix of Gαi1 and a loop protruding from Gβ1, stabilizing the structures.
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: scFv16 interacts with the N-terminal helix of Gαi1 and a loop protruding from Gβ1, stabilizing the structures.
source: In the structure, the C-terminal helix of Gαi1 is inserted inside of the seven transmembrane (TM) helices forming hydrophobic interactions with TM 5–7 helices (Figure 1B), and scFv16 interacts with the N-terminal helix of Gαi1 and a loop protruding from Gβ1, stabilizing the structures.
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The topology and structure of the TM helices is similar to other known GPCRs.
source: The topology and structure of the TM helices is similar to other known GPCRs (Weis and Kobilka, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with known GPCR structures and a citation.

claim: The cryo-EM structure of SSTR2 shows a conventional active conformation, in which TM5, TM6, and TM7 are displaced outward from TM3.
source: Our cryo-EM structure of SSTR2 shows a conventional active conformation, in which TM5, TM6, and TM7 are displaced outward from TM3 (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure and shown in the figures.

claim: The TM helices of SSTR2 at the extracellular side form a pocket for ligands.
source: The TM helices of SSTR2 at the extracellular side form a pocket for ligands, and SST-14 nestles snugly at the pocket (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: SST-14 nestles snugly at the pocket formed by TM helices.
source: The TM helices of SSTR2 at the extracellular side form a pocket for ligands, and SST-14 nestles snugly at the pocket (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Among the 14 amino acids in SST-14, 12 amino acid residues from Cys3 to Cys14 are clearly visible in the cryo-EM map.
source: Among the 14 amino acids in SST-14, 12 amino acid residues from Cys3 to Cys14 are clearly visible in the cryo-EM map, and the positions of the side chains were unambiguously assigned on the map (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the cryo-EM map shown in Figure 2A.

claim: SST-14 is cyclized via a disulfide bond between Cys3 and Cys14.
source: SST-14 is cyclized via a disulfide bond between Cys3 and Cys14, and the region between Phe6 and Phe11 forms a flat sheet (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The region between Phe6 and Phe11 of SST-14 forms a flat sheet.
source: SST-14 is cyclized via a disulfide bond between Cys3 and Cys14, and the region between Phe6 and Phe11 forms a flat sheet (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The disulfide bond of SST-14 is located outward from the ligand-binding pocket of SSTR2.
source: In this configuration, the disulfide bond is located outward from the ligand-binding pocket of SSTR2, and the two amino acids of Trp8 and Lys9 are positioned at the bottom of the binding pocket (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Trp8 and Lys9 of SST-14 are positioned at the bottom of the binding pocket.
source: In this configuration, the disulfide bond is located outward from the ligand-binding pocket of SSTR2, and the two amino acids of Trp8 and Lys9 are positioned at the bottom of the binding pocket (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The binding mode of SST-14 to SSTR2 is similar to those of other cyclic peptides, including oxytocin in OTR and setmelanotide in MC4R.
source: The binding mode of SST-14 to SSTR2 is similar to those of other cyclic peptides, including oxytocin in OTR and setmelanotide in MC4R (Israeli et al., 2021; Meyerowitz et al., 2022; Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison with cited structures and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: Trp9 of SST-14 interacts with SSTR2 via a hydrophobic pocket formed by Ile177, Phe208, Thr212, and Phe272 from TM4–6 helices.
source: At the bottom of the ligand-binding pocket, Trp9 of SST-14 interacts with SSTR2 via a hydrophobic pocket formed by Ile177, Phe208, Thr212, and Phe272 from TM4–6 helices (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Lys9 is the only charged residue among the amino acids of SST-14 located inside of the pocket.
source: Notably, Lys9 is the only charged residue among the amino acids of SST-14, which is located inside of the pocket.
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: Lys9 of SST-14 forms a salt bridge with Asp122 with a 2.7 Å distance.
source: Lys9 of SST-14 forms a salt bridge with Asp122 with a 2.7 Å distance and makes a hydrogen bond with the oxygen atom of the Gln126 side chain.
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure with measured distance.

claim: Lys9 of SST-14 makes a hydrogen bond with the oxygen atom of the Gln126 side chain.
source: Lys9 of SST-14 forms a salt bridge with Asp122 with a 2.7 Å distance and makes a hydrogen bond with the oxygen atom of the Gln126 side chain.
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The carbonyl oxygen in the peptide bond between Lys8 and Trp9 forms a hydrogen bond with Asn276.
source: In addition, the carbonyl oxygen in the peptide bond between Lys8 and Trp9 forms a hydrogen bond with Asn276.
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The Phe275, Leu290, and Phe294 residues of SSTR2 accommodate the Phe6 residue of SST-14.
source: Specifically, the Phe275, Leu290, and Phe294 residues of SSTR2 accommodate the Phe6 residue of SST-14, and the Phe7 residue of SST-14 is stacked on Tyr205 coming from the TM5 helix and further stabilized by the interactions with the Ile195 and Phe208 residues.
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The Phe7 residue of SST-14 is stacked on Tyr205 coming from the TM5 helix.
source: Specifically, the Phe275, Leu290, and Phe294 residues of SSTR2 accommodate the Phe6 residue of SST-14, and the Phe7 residue of SST-14 is stacked on Tyr205 coming from the TM5 helix and further stabilized by the interactions with the Ile195 and Phe208 residues.
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The Phe7 residue of SST-14 is further stabilized by the interactions with the Ile195 and Phe208 residues.
source: Specifically, the Phe275, Leu290, and Phe294 residues of SSTR2 accommodate the Phe6 residue of SST-14, and the Phe7 residue of SST-14 is stacked on Tyr205 coming from the TM5 helix and further stabilized by the interactions with the Ile195 and Phe208 residues.
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: SSTR2D122A showed less than 20% inhibition of cAMP production.
source: While the cAMP production was completely inhibited by SST-14 at submicromolar range concentrations for SSTR2WT, SSTR2D122A showed less than 20% inhibition of cAMP production, indicating that the disruption of the bridge likely abrogated the interaction between SSTR2 and SST-14.
evidence: This is a direct measurement from the functional assay.

claim: The disruption of the salt bridge between Lys9 and Asp122 likely abrogated the interaction between SSTR2 and SST-14.
source: While the cAMP production was completely inhibited by SST-14 at submicromolar range concentrations for SSTR2WT, SSTR2D122A showed less than 20% inhibition of cAMP production, indicating that the disruption of the bridge likely abrogated the interaction between SSTR2 and SST-14.
evidence: This is inferred from the functional assay results comparing WT and D122A mutant.

claim: Mutating Gln126 to Met substantially decreased the function of SSTR2.
source: Next, we mutated Gln126 to methionine and examined its effect. Gln126 forms a hydrogen bond with Lys9 of SST-14 in addition to the salt bridge, and mutating Gln to Met substantially decreased the function of SSTR2.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the functional assay.

claim: Among the five isoforms, SSTR2, SSTR3, and SSTR5 isoforms have glutamine while SSTR1 and SSTR4 have methionines at position 126.
source: Notably, among the five isoforms, SSTR2, SSTR3, and SSTR5 isoforms have glutamine while SSTR1 and SSTR4 have methionines at this position.
evidence: This is based on sequence alignment analysis.

claim: Eliminating the hydrophobic interactions between SST-14 and SSTR2 by mutating Phe272 or Phe294 to alanines substantially decreased the function of SSTR2.
source: We further examined the effects of the hydrophobic residues interacting with SST-14 by mutating Phe272 or Phe294 to alanines. Eliminating the hydrophobic interactions between SST-14 and SSTR2 also substantially decreased the function of SSTR2, emphasizing their roles in recognizing its ligand.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the functional assay.

claim: The endogenous agonists for SSTRs are SST-14 and SST-28.
source: The endogenous agonists for SSTRs are SST-14 and SST-28 (Patel et al., 1994; Patel and Srikant, 1994).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: SST-28 has an extra 14 residues at the N-terminus compared to SST-14.
source: Compared to SST-14, SST-28 has an extra 14 residues at the N-terminus (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is shown in the sequence alignment in Figure 3A.

claim: The region of SST-14 is likely sufficient for binding to SSTR2.
source: Our cryo-EM structure shows that the region of SST-14 is likely sufficient for binding to SSTR2.
evidence: This is inferred from the cryo-EM structure showing complete binding of SST-14.

claim: SST-28 has a binding affinity similar to that of SST-14, in the subnanomolar range.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, SST-28 has a binding affinity similar to that of SST-14, in the subnanomolar range (Song et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: All SSTR2-binding ligands and drugs are cyclic forms of peptides and contain absolutely conserved Trp and Lys residues.
source: In addition to SST-14, there are several other ligands and drugs that bind to SSTR2, including cortistatin, octreotide, pasireotide, and lanreotide. All of these ligands and drugs are cyclic forms of peptides and contain absolutely conserved Trp and Lys residues (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is shown in the sequence alignment in Figure 3A.

claim: The Trp-Lys motif of the ligands and drugs is likely a major determinant for binding.
source: The interaction analysis based on the cryo-EM structure showed that these highly conserved Trp and Lys residues tightly interact with SSTR2 via hydrophobic interactions and a salt bridge. Therefore, it is likely that the Trp-Lys motif of the ligands and drugs is a major determinant for binding.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural analysis and sequence conservation.

claim: There are five isoforms of SSTRs (SSTR1–5), which are classified into two families based on their structural and pharmacological properties.
source: There are five isoforms of SSTRs (SSTR1–5), which are classified into two families based on their structural and pharmacological properties.
evidence: This is established knowledge about SSTR classification.

claim: SSTR2, SSTR3, and SSTR5 belong to the SRIF1 receptor family.
source: SSTR2, SSTR3, and SSTR5 belong to the SRIF1 receptor family, and SSTR1 and SSTR4 belong to the SRIF2 receptor family (Günther et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: SSTR1 and SSTR4 belong to the SRIF2 receptor family.
source: SSTR2, SSTR3, and SSTR5 belong to the SRIF1 receptor family, and SSTR1 and SSTR4 belong to the SRIF2 receptor family (Günther et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The tissues that express each isoform and its cognate ligand differ, implying the isoform-specific function of SSTRs.
source: The tissues that express each isoform and its cognate ligand differ, implying the isoform-specific function of SSTRs (Song et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The residues involved in interacting with the Trp-Lys motif are highly conserved among SSTR isoforms.
source: This practice revealed that the residues involved in interacting with the Trp-Lys motif are highly conserved.
evidence: This is based on sequence alignment analysis combined with structural data.

claim: The residues interacting with the other part of SST-14 are highly variable among SSTR isoforms.
source: On the other hand, the residues interacting with the other part of SST-14 are highly variable, suggesting that this region contributes to the ligand specificity among SSTR isoforms.
evidence: This is based on sequence alignment analysis combined with structural data.

claim: The variable region contributes to the ligand specificity among SSTR isoforms.
source: On the other hand, the residues interacting with the other part of SST-14 are highly variable, suggesting that this region contributes to the ligand specificity among SSTR isoforms.

claim: SSTR2, SSTR3, and SSTR5 likely have different binding characteristics than SSTR1 and SSTR4.
source: Collectively, our structural and sequence analyses suggest that SSTR2, SSTR3, and SSTR5 likely have different binding characteristics than SSTR1 and SSTR4.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural and sequence analysis.

claim: Octreotide, lanreotide, and pasireotide have higher affinities toward SSTR2, SSTR3, and SSTR5 than SSTR1 and SSTR4.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, octreotide, lanreotide, and pasireotide have higher affinities toward SSTR2, SSTR3, and SSTR5 than SSTR1 and SSTR4 (Song et al., 2021; Barbieri et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Extracellular loop 2 (ECL2) and ECL3 are involved in ligand-specific binding among SSTR isoforms.
source: A recent report on the SSTR2 structure by Robertson et al. showed that extracellular loop 2 (ECL2) and ECL3 are involved in ligand-specific binding among SSTR isoforms, which have highly variable sequences among the SSTR isoforms (Figure 3B; Robertson et al., 2022).

claim: ECL2 and ECL3 have highly variable sequences among the SSTR isoforms.
source: A recent report on the SSTR2 structure by Robertson et al. showed that extracellular loop 2 (ECL2) and ECL3 are involved in ligand-specific binding among SSTR isoforms, which have highly variable sequences among the SSTR isoforms (Figure 3B; Robertson et al., 2022).
evidence: This is shown in the sequence alignment in Figure 3B and supported by citation.

claim: The interactions between the ligands and SSTR2 at the inside of the binding pocket are critical for the ligand specificity.
source: In addition, consistent with our findings, they also showed that the interactions between the ligands and SSTR2 at the inside of the binding pocket are also critical for the ligand specificity.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to recent research and is consistent with the authors' findings.

claim: Several regions of SSTR2 including residues in the ECLs and the inside of the binding pockets likely contribute to the ligand-binding specificity.
source: Therefore, several regions of SSTR2 including residues in the ECLs and the inside of the binding pockets likely contribute to the ligand-binding specificity.

claim: The cryo-EM map was well resolved, and the atomic model for most part of the SSTR2 complex was built on the map.
source: The cryo-EM map was well resolved, and the atomic model for most part of the SSTR2 complex was built on the map (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a statement about the quality of the cryo-EM data and model building.

claim: The complete complex of SSTR2, heterotrimeric Gαi1/Gβ1γ2, and scFv16 was eluted at the first peak around 11.25 mL in size exclusion chromatography.
